questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\lim (\sec \theta-\tan \theta)$ equal to? $x \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{2}$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} &  \lim _{\theta \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{2}}(\sec \theta-\tan \theta) \\ & \lim _{\theta \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{2}}(\sec \theta-\tan \theta)=\lim _{\theta \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{1-\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}\left(\frac{0}{0} \text { form }\right) \\ & \lim _{\theta \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\frac{-\cos \theta}{-\sin \theta}\right)=0 \text { (Using L Hospital Rule) }\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let the function $f(x) = x^2 + 9$.

What is $\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\sqrt{f(x)} - 3}{\sqrt{f(x)+7} - 4}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = x^2 + 9$.

The limit is $\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2 + 9} - 3}{\sqrt{x^2 + 16} - 4}$.

Rationalizing the numerator and the denominator:

$\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{(\sqrt{x^2 + 9} - 3)(\sqrt{x^2 + 9} + 3)}{(\sqrt{x^2 + 16} - 4)(\sqrt{x^2 + 16} + 4)} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2 + 16} + 4}{\sqrt{x^2 + 9} + 3}$

$\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{x^2 + 9 - 9}{x^2 + 16 - 16} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2 + 16} + 4}{\sqrt{x^2 + 9} + 3}$

$\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{x^2}{x^2} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2 + 16} + 4}{\sqrt{x^2 + 9} + 3}$

Cancelling $x^2$ and substituting $x = 0$:

$\dfrac{\sqrt{16} + 4}{\sqrt{9} + 3} = \dfrac{4 + 4}{3 + 3} = \dfrac{8}{6} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{4}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Which one of the following is correct regarding $\lim _{x \rightarrow 3} \frac{|x-3|}{x-3} ?$
options: Limits exists and is equal to 1
Limits exists and is equal to 0
Limits exists and is equal to -1
questions.solution:
Given,
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 3} \frac{|x-3|}{x-3}$
Finding LRL and RHL at $x=3\mathrm{LHL}=\operatorname{lt}_{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow 3^{-}} \frac{|\mathrm{x}-3|}{\mathrm{x}-3}=\frac{-(\mathrm{x}-3)}{\mathrm{x}-3}=-1\mathrm{LHL}=\operatorname{lt}_{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow 3^{+}} \frac{|\mathrm{x}-3|}{\mathrm{x}-3}=\frac{(\mathrm{x}-3)}{\mathrm{x}-3}=+1$
LHL ≠ RHL, limit does not exist.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
For the following three (03) items:
Consider the function $f(x) = x|x|$.

What is $\lim_{x \to -1} f(x)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given the function $f(x) = x|x|$.

We need to evaluate $\lim_{x \to -1} f(x)$.

Since $x$ approaches $-1$, $x$ is negative, so $|x| = -x$.

Thus, $f(x) = x(-x) = -x^2$ for $x \lt 0$.

$\lim_{x \to -1} f(x) = \lim_{x \to -1} (-x^2) = -(-1)^2 = -1$.

Answer: $-1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\lim\limits_{x\to1}\dfrac{x^{(n^2-1)}-1}{x^{(n+1)}-1}$ equal to, where $n\gt 1$ is a natural number ?
questions.solution:
The given limit is $\lim\limits_{x\to1}\dfrac{x^{(n^2-1)}-1}{x^{(n+1)}-1}$.

As $x \to 1$, the expression takes the indeterminate form $\dfrac{0}{0}$.

Applying L'Hospital's rule, we differentiate the numerator and the denominator with respect to $x$:

$\lim\limits_{x\to1}\dfrac{(n^2-1)x^{n^2-2}}{(n+1)x^n}$

Substituting $x=1$, we get:

$\dfrac{n^2-1}{n+1}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{(n-1)(n+1)}{n+1}$

$\Rightarrow n-1$

Answer: $n-1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\lim\limits_{x\to0}\dfrac{10^{\sin x}-1}{\tan x}$ equal to ?
questions.solution:
The given limit is $\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{10^{\sin x}-1}{\tan x}$

Multiplying and dividing the expression by $\sin x$:

$\lim_{x\to0}\left(\dfrac{10^{\sin x}-1}{\sin x} \times \dfrac{\sin x}{\tan x}\right)$

$\lim_{x\to0}\left(\dfrac{10^{\sin x}-1}{\sin x} \times \cos x\right)$

Using the standard limit $\lim_{t\to0}\dfrac{a^t-1}{t} = \ln a$, where $t = \sin x \to 0$ as $x \to 0$:

$\ln 10 \times \cos 0$

$\ln 10 \times 1 = \ln 10$

Answer: $\ln 10$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
For the following two (02) items:
Let $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1 - \cos 2x}{x^2}, & x \lt 0 \\ 9, & x = 0 \\ \dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{(16 + \sqrt{x})} - 4}, & x \gt 0 \end{cases}$

What is $\lim_{x \to 0^-} f(x)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
For $x \lt 0$, the function is given by $f(x) = \dfrac{1 - \cos 2x}{x^2}$

To find the left-hand limit, we evaluate $\lim_{x \to 0^-} f(x)$

$\lim_{x \to 0^-} \dfrac{1 - \cos 2x}{x^2}$

Using the trigonometric identity $1 - \cos 2x = 2 \sin^2 x$

$\lim_{x \to 0^-} \dfrac{2 \sin^2 x}{x^2} = 2 \left( \lim_{x \to 0^-} \dfrac{\sin x}{x} \right)^2$

Since $\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\sin x}{x} = 1$, we get:

$2 \times (1)^2 = 2$

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Let $f(x) \quad \frac{a^{x-1} b^{x-1}}{}$ and $g(x)=x-1$.
What is $\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{f(x)-1}{g(x)}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Since, $\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{f(x)-1}{g(x)}\begin{aligned}
& =\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{\frac{a^{x-1}+b^{x-1}}{2}-1}{x-1}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{a^{x-1}+b^{x-1}-2}{2(x-1)} \\
& =\lim _{x \rightarrow 1}\left(\frac{a^{x-1}-1}{2(x-1)}+\frac{b^{x-1}-1}{2(x-1)}\right)=\frac{1}{2} \ln a+\frac{1}{2} \ln (b) \\
& =\frac{1}{2} \ln (a b)
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: What is $\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{x^9-1}{x^3-1}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{x^9-1}{x^3-1}\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{\left(x^3\right)^3-1}{x^3-1}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{\left(x^3-1\right)\left(x^6+x^3+1\right)}{x^3-1}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} x^6+x^3+1=3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f(x)=\frac{x 2+x+|x|}{x}$ then what is $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} f(x)$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { L.H.L. }=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}}=\frac{x^2+x-x}{x}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} x=0 \\ & \text {R.H.L. }=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} \frac{x^2+2 x}{x}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} x+2=2 \\ & \because \quad \text { L.H.L } \neq \text { R.H.L. } \\ & \therefore \quad \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} f(x) \text { does not exist. }\end{aligned}$

questions.q: What is $\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin ^2(x+h)-\sin ^2 x}{h}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin ^2(x+h)-\sin ^2 x}{h}$
Apply L' Hospital rule

$=\sin 2 x$

questions.q: What is $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} x^3(\operatorname{cosec} x)^2$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} x^3(\operatorname{cosec} x)^2 \\ & =\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{x^3}{\sin ^2 x}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{x}{\sin x}\right)^2 \cdot x \\ & =1.0=0\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{x^3-1}{\sqrt{x}-1}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{x^3-1}{\sqrt{x}-1}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{\left(x^3-1\right)(\sqrt{x}+1)}{x-1} \\ & =\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{(x-1)\left(x^2+x+1\right)(\sqrt{x}+1)}{x-1} \\ & =(1+1+1)(1+1)=6\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{a^n+b^n}{a^n-b^n}$ where $a \gt b \gt 1$, equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{a^n+b^n}{a^n-b^n} \\ & \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{a^n\left[1+\left(\frac{b}{a}\right)^n\right]}{a^n\left[1-\left(\frac{b}{a}\right)^n\right]} \\ & a \gt b \gt 1 \\ & a \gt b \Rightarrow \frac{a}{b} \gt 1\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & a \gt b \Rightarrow \frac{a}{b} \lt 1 \\ & =\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\left[1+\left(\frac{b}{a}\right)^n\right]}{\left[1-\left(\frac{b}{a}\right)^n\right]}=\frac{1+0}{1-0} \\ & \therefore \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{a^n+b^n}{a^n-b^n}=1\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f(x)=\frac{|x|}{|x|}, x \neq 0$, where [.] denotes the greatest integer function, then what is the right-hand limit of $f(x)$ at $x=1$ ?
options: Right-hand limit of $f(x)$ at $x=1$ does not exist
questions.solution:
$f(x)=\frac{[x]}{|x|}= \begin{cases}\frac{[x]}{-x}, & x \lt 0 \\ \frac{[x]}{x} & , x \geq 0\end{cases}$
Right hand limit of $f(x)$ at $x=1$,
$\mathrm{RHL}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{[x]}{x}=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{[1+h]}{1+h}=1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\lim _{x \rightarrow-1} \frac{x^3+x^2}{x^2+3 x+2}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\lim _{x \rightarrow-1} \frac{x^3+x^2}{x^2+3 x+2}$
By L'Hospital rule,
$\lim _{x \rightarrow-1} \frac{3 x^2+2 x}{2 x+3}=\frac{3(-1)^2+2(-1)}{2(-1)+3}=\frac{3-2}{-2+3}=1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\lim _{x \rightarrow a} \frac{a^x-x^a}{x^a-a^a}=-1$ then what is the value of $a$ ?
questions.solution:
$\lim _{x \rightarrow a} \frac{a^x-x^a}{x^a-a^a}$
This is in $\frac{0}{0}$ form, by L'Hospital rule
$\lim _{x \rightarrow a} \frac{a^x-x^a}{x^a-a^a}=\lim _{x \rightarrow a} \frac{a^x \cdot \ln a-a \cdot x^{a-1}}{a \cdot x^{a-1}-0}=\frac{a^a \cdot \ln a-a^a}{a^a}=\ln a-1$.
$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \ln a-1=-1 \Rightarrow \ln a=0 \\ & \therefore a=(e)^0=1 .\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
For the following two (02) items:
Let $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1 - \cos 2x}{x^2}, & x \lt 0 \\ 9, & x = 0 \\ \dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{(16 + \sqrt{x})} - 4}, & x \gt 0 \end{cases}$

What is $\lim_{x \to 0^+} f(x)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
For $x \gt 0$, the function is given by $f(x) = \dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{16 + \sqrt{x}} - 4}$

To find the right-hand limit, we evaluate $\lim_{x \to 0^+} f(x)$

$\lim_{x \to 0^+} \dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{16 + \sqrt{x}} - 4}$

Rationalizing the denominator by multiplying the numerator and the denominator by $\sqrt{16 + \sqrt{x}} + 4$:

$\lim_{x \to 0^+} \dfrac{\sqrt{x}(\sqrt{16 + \sqrt{x}} + 4)}{(\sqrt{16 + \sqrt{x}} - 4)(\sqrt{16 + \sqrt{x}} + 4)}$

$\lim_{x \to 0^+} \dfrac{\sqrt{x}(\sqrt{16 + \sqrt{x}} + 4)}{16 + \sqrt{x} - 16}$

$\lim_{x \to 0^+} \dfrac{\sqrt{x}(\sqrt{16 + \sqrt{x}} + 4)}{\sqrt{x}}$

Canceling $\sqrt{x}$ from the numerator and the denominator:

$\lim_{x \to 0^+} (\sqrt{16 + \sqrt{x}} + 4)$

Substituting $x = 0$:

$\sqrt{16 + 0} + 4 = 4 + 4 = 8$

Answer: $8$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let the function $f(x) = \sin[x]$, where $[\cdot]$ is the greatest integer function and $g(x) = |x|$.

What is $\lim_{x \to 0} \{f(x) g(x)\}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = \sin[x]$ and $g(x) = |x|$.

To find $\lim_{x \to 0} f(x) g(x)$, we evaluate the left-hand limit (LHL) and the right-hand limit (RHL).

For LHL, as $x \to 0^{-}$, $[x] = -1$ and $|x| = -x$.

$\lim_{x \to 0^{-}} f(x) g(x) = \lim_{x \to 0^{-}} (\sin(-1))(-x) = (-\sin 1)(0) = 0$

For RHL, as $x \to 0^{+}$, $[x] = 0$ and $|x| = x$.

$\lim_{x \to 0^{+}} f(x) g(x) = \lim_{x \to 0^{+}} (\sin 0)(x) = (0)(0) = 0$

Since LHL = RHL = $0$, the limit exists and is equal to $0$.

Answer: $0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let the function $f(x) = \sin[x]$, where $[\cdot]$ is the greatest integer function and $g(x) = |x|$.

What is $\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
The given functions are $f(x) = \sin[x]$ and $g(x) = |x|$.

To find $\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}$, we evaluate the left-hand limit (LHL) and right-hand limit (RHL) at $x = 0$.

For the right-hand limit ($x \to 0^+$):
When $0 \lt x \lt 1$, $[x] = 0$ and $|x| = x$.
$\lim_{x \to 0^+} \dfrac{\sin[x]}{|x|} = \lim_{x \to 0^+} \dfrac{\sin 0}{x} = \lim_{x \to 0^+} \dfrac{0}{x} = 0$

For the left-hand limit ($x \to 0^-$):
When $-1 \lt x \lt 0$, $[x] = -1$ and $|x| = -x$.
$\lim_{x \to 0^-} \dfrac{\sin[x]}{|x|} = \lim_{x \to 0^-} \dfrac{\sin(-1)}{-x} = \lim_{x \to 0^-} \dfrac{-\sin 1}{-x} = \lim_{x \to 0^-} \dfrac{\sin 1}{x} = -\infty$

Since the left-hand limit and right-hand limit are not equal, the limit does not exist.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let the function $f(x) = x^2 - 1$.

What is $\lim_{x \to 1} \{f \circ f(x)\}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = x^2 - 1$.

The composite function $f \circ f(x)$ is given by:

$f(f(x)) = f(x^2 - 1) = (x^2 - 1)^2 - 1$

Since $f(f(x))$ is a polynomial and continuous everywhere, the limit can be evaluated by direct substitution:

$\lim_{x \to 1} \{f \circ f(x)\} = f(f(1))$

$f(1) = 1^2 - 1 = 0$

$f(f(1)) = f(0) = 0^2 - 1 = -1$

Thus, the limit is $-1$.

Answer: $-1$

Let $f(x)=|x|+1$ and $g(x)=[x]-1$, where [.] is the greatest integer function.
Let $h(x)=\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}$
What is $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0-} h(x)+\lim _{x \rightarrow 0+} h(x)$ equal to?
questions.solution: and $\begin{aligned} f(x) & =|x|+1 \\ g(x) & =[x]-1 \\ h(x) & =\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}=\frac{|x|+1}{[x]-1}\end{aligned}\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} h(x)+\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} h(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} \frac{|x|+1}{[x]-1}\begin{array}{ll}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} \frac{|x|+1}{[x]-1} & \\ =\frac{0+1}{-1-1}+\frac{0+1}{0-1} & \left\{\begin{array}{l}{[0-h]=-1} \\ {[0+h]=0}\end{array}\right\} \\ =\frac{1}{2}-1=-\frac{3}{2} & \end{array}$

$=\frac{3^0 \cdot \log 3-3^0 \cdot \log 3}{1}=0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
If a differentiable function $f(x)$ satisfies
$\lim _{x \rightarrow-1} \frac{f(x)+1}{x^2-1}=-\frac{3}{2}$
then what is $\lim _{x \rightarrow-1} f(x)$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \lim _{x \rightarrow-1} \frac{f(x)+1}{x^2-1}=\frac{-3}{2} \\ & {\left[\frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{2 x}\right]=\frac{-3}{2}}\end{aligned}$
On integrating both sides,
$\begin{aligned} & f(x)=\frac{-3}{2} x^2+c \quad \text { where } c=\text { Constant } \\ & \lim _{x \rightarrow-1} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow-1}\left[\frac{-3}{2} x^2+c\right]=\frac{-3}{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{x+x^2+x^3-3}{x-1}$ equal to ?
questions.solution:
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{x+x^2+x^3-3}{x-1}$
This is in $\frac{0}{0}$ form, so we can use L' Hospital rule.
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{x+x^2+x^3-3}{x-1}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{1+2 x+3 x^2}{1}=\frac{1+2+3}{1}=6$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the function $f(x)=\frac{2 x-\sin ^{-1} x}{2 x+\tan ^{-1} x}$ is continuous at each point in its domain, then what is the value of $f(0)$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & f(0)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{2 x-\sin ^{-1} x}{2 x+\tan ^{-1} x} \\ & =\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{2-\frac{\sin ^{-1} x}{x}}{2+\frac{\tan ^{-1} x}{x}}=\frac{2-1}{2+1}=\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin x \log (1-x)}{x^2}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin x \cdot \log (1-x)}{x^2}$
This is in $\frac{0}{0}$ form, by using L' Hospital rule.
$\begin{aligned} & \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin x \cdot \log (1-x)}{x^2} \\ & =\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\cos x \cdot \log (1-x)+\sin x \cdot \frac{1}{(1-x)}(-1)}{2 x}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\log (1-x) \cdot(-\sin x)-\frac{\cos x}{(1-x)}-\frac{1}{(1-x)} \cdot \cos x-\frac{\sin x}{(1-x)^2}}{2} \\ & =\frac{0-1-1-0}{2}=\frac{-2}{2}=-1\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{x^4-1}{x-1}=\lim _{x \rightarrow k} \frac{x^3-k^3}{x^2-k^2}$, where $k \neq 0$, then what is the value of $k$ ?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{x^4-1}{x-1} & =\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} \frac{(x-1)(x+1)\left(x^2+1\right)}{(x-1)} \\
& =\lim _{x \rightarrow 1}(x+1)\left(x^2+1\right)=(1+1)(1+1)=4
\end{aligned}$
Now, $\lim _{x \rightarrow k} \frac{x^3-k^3}{x^2-k^2}=4\lim _{x \rightarrow k} \frac{(x-k)\left(x^2+k^2+x k\right)}{(x-k)(x+k)}=4\begin{aligned} & \lim _{x \rightarrow k} \frac{\left(x^2+k^2+x k\right)}{(x+k)}=4 \\ & \frac{k^2+k^2+k \cdot k}{k+k}=4 \Rightarrow \frac{3}{2} k=4 \Rightarrow k=\frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1-\cos ^3 4 x}{x^2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{1-\cos ^3 4 x}{x^2}$
The given limit is in $\frac{0}{0}$ form. So, apply L'hospital rule.
$\begin{aligned} & \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{-3 \cos ^2 4 x(-\sin 4 x) 4}{2 x} \\ & =\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{12 \cos ^2 4 x \sin 4 x}{(2 x) 2} \times 2 \\ & =24 \cdot \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \cos ^2 4 x \cdot \frac{\sin 4 x}{4 x} \\ & =24(1)=24\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\lim _{x \rightarrow 5} \frac{5-x}{|x-5|}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\lim _{x \rightarrow 5} \frac{5-x}{|x-5|}$
LHL: $\lim _{x \rightarrow 5^{-}} \frac{5-x}{-(x-5)}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 5^{-}} \frac{5-x}{5-x}=1$
RHL: $\lim _{x \rightarrow 5^{+}} \frac{5-x}{(x-5)}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 5^{+}}(-1)=-1\therefore \quad$ LHL ≠ RHL $\therefore$ Limit does not exist.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{\sin x}{x}=l$ and $\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\cos x}{x}=m$, then which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{\sin x}{x}=l \text { and } \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\cos x}{x}=m \\ & \lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{\sin x}{x}=\frac{1}{\frac{\pi}{2}}=\frac{2}{\pi} ; \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\cos x}{x}=0\end{aligned}\therefore l=\frac{2}{\pi}, \mathrm{~m}=0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sqrt{2 x+3 h}-\sqrt{2 x}}{2 h}$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Let $L=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sqrt{2 x+3 h}-\sqrt{2 x}}{2 h}$
Rationalise the numerator, we get:
$L=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2 x+3 h}-\sqrt{2 x}}{2 h} \times \frac{\sqrt{2 x+3 h}+\sqrt{2 x}}{\sqrt{2 x+3 h}+\sqrt{2 x}}\right)\begin{aligned} & =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{2 x+3 h-2 x}{2 h(\sqrt{2 x+3 h}+\sqrt{2 x})} \\ & =\frac{3}{2(\sqrt{2 x+0}+\sqrt{2 x})}=\frac{3}{4 \sqrt{2 x}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
Let $f(x)=|x|$ and $g(x)=[x]-1$, where [.] is the greatest integer function.

What is $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0-} h(x)$ equal to?
questions.solution: Since, $h(x)=\frac{f(g(x))}{g(f(x))}=\frac{f([x]-1)}{g(|x|)}=\frac{|[x]-1|}{[|x|]-1}\begin{aligned} & \text { Since, }=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0-} h(x) \\ & =\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} \frac{|[x]-1|}{[x]-1}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}}=\frac{|-1-1|}{-1}=-2\end{aligned}$

$\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{e^x-(1+x)}{x^2}=\frac{1}{2} \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{e^x-1}{x}=\frac{1}{2} \times 1=\frac{1}{2} .$

It is $\frac{0}{0}$ (undefined) condition so using L'hospital's rule

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Given that $\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{2+x^2}{1+x}-A x-B\right)=3$.
What is the value of A?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{2+\mathrm{x}^2}{1+\mathrm{x}}-\mathrm{Ax}-\mathrm{B}\right)=3 \\
\Rightarrow & \lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{2+\mathrm{x}^2-\mathrm{Ax}-\mathrm{B}-\mathrm{Ax}^2-\mathrm{Bx}}{1+\mathrm{x}}\right)=3 \\
\Rightarrow & \lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow \infty}\left[\frac{(1-\mathrm{A}) \mathrm{x}^2-(\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}) \mathrm{x}+2-\mathrm{B}}{1+\mathrm{x}}\right]=3
\end{aligned}$
Applying L'Hospital rule,
$2 x(1-A)-(A+B)=3$
Comparing coefficients
$\begin{array}{ll} 
& 2(1-A)=0 \\
\therefore \quad & A=1 \text { and } \\
& -(A+B)=3 \\
\therefore \quad & B=-3-1=-4 \\
& A+B=-3 \\
& A=1 . B=-4
\end{array}$

questions.q: What is $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{(1+x)^n-1}{x}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{(1+x)^n-1}{x} \\ & \frac{(1+x)^1-1}{x}=\frac{1+x-1}{x}=\frac{x}{x}=1 \\ & \frac{(1+x)^2-1}{x}=\frac{1+2 x+x^2-1}{x}=\frac{x(2+x)}{x}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \frac{(1+x)^3-1}{x} & =\frac{1+3 x+3 x^2+x^3-1}{x} \\ & =\frac{3 x+3 x^2+x^3}{x}=\frac{x\left(3+3 x+x^2\right)}{x} \\ \therefore \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{(1+x)^n-1}{x} & =\frac{1+n \cdot x+\ldots-1}{x} \\ & =\frac{n x+\text { highest power of } x}{x} \\ & =\frac{x(n+\text { highest power of } x)}{x} \\ & =n+\text { highest power of } x \\ & =n\end{aligned}$

2. If $\lim _{x \rightarrow a}\{f(x) g(x)\}$ exists, then both $\lim _{x \rightarrow a} f(x)$ and $\lim _{x \rightarrow a} g(x)$ must exist.
Which of the above statements is correct?
questions.solution: If $\lim _{x \rightarrow a} f(x)$ and $\lim _{x \rightarrow a} g(x)$ both exists, then $\lim _{x \rightarrow a} f(x) \cdot g(x)$ exists. But if $\lim _{x \rightarrow a} f(x) \cdot g(x)$ exists, then it is not necesary that both $\lim _{x \rightarrow a} f(x)$ and $\lim _{x \rightarrow a} g(x)$ exists.

questions.q:
Paragraph: Let $f(x)=[x]$, where [.] is the greatest integer function and $g(x)=\sin x$ be two real valued functions over $R$.
Question: Which one of the following statements is correct?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& (f \circ g)(x)=[\sin x] \\
& \lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}}(f o g)(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}}[\sin x]=[h] \text { where } h \gt 0 \\
& \Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}}(f o g)(x)=0 \\
& \lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}}(f \circ g)(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}}[\sin x]=[h] \text { where } h \lt 0 \\
& \Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}}(f o g)(x)=-1 \\
& \Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow 0}(f o g)(x) \text { does not exist. }
\end{aligned}$
Now, $(g o f)(x)=\sin [x]\begin{aligned}
& \lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}}(g o f)(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} \sin [x]=\sin 0=0 \\
& \lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}}(g o f)(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} \sin [x]=\sin (-1)=-0.01745 \\
& \Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow 0}(g o f)(x) \text { does not exist. } \\
& \Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}}(f o g)(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}}(g o f)(x)
\end{aligned}$
